Paragraph:
Translation: My dear Arjuna, a man who does not follow this prescribed Vedic system of sacrifice certainly leads a life of sin, for a person delighting only in the senses lives in vain.

Purport (Excerpt): The mammonist philosophy of work very hard and enjoy sense gratification is condemned herein by the Lord... One who does not follow such regulations is living a very risky life... By nature's law, this human form of life is specifically meant for self-realization... satisfy their desires without becoming entangled in the reaction of sense-gratificatory work.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Living a self-indulgent life focused exclusively on sensory enjoyment while ignoring the cosmic cycles of contribution and duty.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna warns that rejecting reciprocal sacrifice to live only for sensory pleasure results in a wasted, harmful life. Following established systems of sacrifice purifies desires and prevents karmic entanglement.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is shown the futility and danger of living solely for egoic indulgence.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Hedonic Treadmill: Chasing unending sensory pleasures without achieving lasting satisfaction
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purpose vs. Indulgence: Balancing personal pleasure with meaningful contribution
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Ethical Accountability: Recognizing the personal and environmental costs of selfish behavior

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Mogham partha sa jivati (Living in vain by existing only for sensory pleasure)
Indriyarama (One whose sole delight is in sensory gratification)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Anyone who fails to participate in the cosmic cycle of sacrifice and instead lives purely for sense gratification lives a sinful, empty existence. The human form of life is designed for self-realization; indulging without sacrifice leads to spiritual failure.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: A life centered strictly on immediate sensory gratification leads to empty hedonism. Chasing constant pleasure without broader purpose or contribution causes psychological burnout, loss of meaning, and existential regret.
